facts.statement: Inawentu was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Santonian age of the Late Cretaceous in Argentina.
facts.quote: Inawentu () is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian age) Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Inawentu possessed a square-shaped jaw showing convergent characteristics with rebbachisaurids.
facts.quote: The square-shaped jaw of Inawentu demonstrates convergent characteristics with rebbachisaurids.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MAU-Pv-LI-595 was discovered near Rincón de los Sauces in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The Inawentu holotype specimen, MAU-Pv-LI-595, was discovered in sediments of the Bajo de la Carpa Formation (Neuquén Group) near Rincón de los Sauces in Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The known fossil material includes a partial articulated skeleton with a nearly complete skull, twelve cervical vertebrae, ten dorsal vertebrae, six sacral vertebrae, and both ilia.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a partial articulated skeleton, including a nearly complete skull, all of the vertebrae from the atlas to the end of the sacrum (comprising twelve cervical, ten dorsal, and six sacral vertebrae), and both ilia.

facts.statement: Filippi et al. announced Inawentu oslatus as a new genus and species in 2023 based on a preprint.
facts.quote: In 2023, Filippi et al. announced Inawentu oslatus as a new genus and species of titanosaurian sauropod based on these fossil remains in a non-final preprint.

facts.statement: Highly modified centra and neural arches suggest Inawentu's neck was capable of multidirectional movement.
facts.quote: The centra and neural arches of the neck and back vertebrae are highly modified, which suggests that the neck would have been capable of multidirectional movement.

facts.statement: Inawentu had narrower hips than Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus.
facts.quote: The hips were narrower than in Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus.

facts.statement: Filippi et al. (2024) recovered Inawentu as the sister taxon to Antarctosaurus in a clade containing Bonitasaura.
facts.quote: Filippi et al. (2024) recovered Inawentu as the sister taxon to Antarctosaurus in a clade also containing the coeval Bonitasaura.

facts.statement: Filippi et al. placed Inawentu in a previously unrecognized clade of square-jawed eutitanosaurs they named "Clade A".
facts.quote: This clade was found to be a member of a previously unrecognized clade of square-jawed eutitanosaurs, which the researchers referred to as "Clade A".

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Filippi et al. placed Inawentu + Antarctosaurus as the sister to Brasilotitan within a basal lineage of Colossosauria.
facts.quote: In 2026, Filippi and colleagues described Yeneen, another titanosaur from the Bajo de la Carpa Formation. Using a novel phylogenetic matrix developed from their description of Inawentu, the researchers recovered a notably different arrangement of taxa, with Inawentu + Antarctosaurus as the sister to Brasilotitan, and this clade instead placed as a basal lineage of the Colossosauria (the clade including the Lognkosauria).

facts.statement: Under equal weights, Inawentu was recovered within Aeolosaurini alongside Gondwanatitan.
facts.quote: Under equal weights, Inawentu shifted to a position within Aeolosaurini alongside Gondwanatitan.

facts.statement: Soto Núñez et al. (2026) regarded Inawentu as a probable aeolosaurine based on a matrix used in the description of Mesetasaurus.
facts.quote: This classification was replicated in the 2026 description of Mesetasaurus by Soto Núñez et al. (2026), who used this matrix and regarded Inawentu as a "probable aeolosaurine".

facts.statement: Inawentu lived approximately 83 million years ago during the Santonian age in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 83 millones de años, durante el Santoniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Inawentu's skull showed convergent similarities to rebbachisaurids like Nigersaurus and Lavocatisaurus, including a wide, squared-off snout deflected strongly downward.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Inawentu mostró varias similitudes convergentes con rebaquisáuridos como Nigersaurus y Lavocatisaurus, como un hocico ancho y cuadrado que se desviaba fuertemente hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Inawentu is ecologically significant for its evolutionary convergence with rebbachisaurids, a group already extinct by this period.
facts.quote: La importancia ecológica de Inawentu radica en las convergencias evolutivas que presenta con los rebachisaurios, un grupo de saurópodos que ya se encontraba extinto para este período.

facts.statement: The genus Inawentu was named by Filippi and colleagues in 2024.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Inawentu (genus), Filippi et al. 2024

facts.statement: Inawentu belongs to the parent group Eutitanosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eutitanosauria

facts.statement: Inawentu is classified within the dinosaur class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Inawentu lived during the Santonian stage, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Inawentu has been recorded so far.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

rejected.quote: MAU-Pv-LI-595 is one of the few known titanosaur specimens to preserve a complete neck.

rejected.statement: Pérez Moreno et al. (2026) recovered Inawentu as the sister taxon to Narambuenatitan within a derived position in Lognkosauria under extended implied weights.
rejected.quote: Under extended implied weights, Inawentu was recovered as the sister taxon to Narambuenatitan, with this clade as the sister to Aeolosaurini + Rinconsauria, which was instead placed in a derived position within Lognkosauria, contrasting with results by Filippi and colleagues.
